title: Federation host-utilization API: Central reads each enrolled host's current CPU, memory, disk and network without manual SSH
outcome: Central can read, through the existing authenticated federation link, a current utilization snapshot of every enrolled host (central and satellites): CPU, memory, disk and network. Each metric has a defined unit, the host's measurement time and an explicit state of available, stale, unavailable or unsupported, so an operator or coordinator never mistakes missing or old data for a fresh reading, and needs no manual SSH.
acceptance: A read-only snapshot endpoint on each host, and a Central aggregate that fetches each enrolled peer's snapshot over the existing authenticated federation link (no new transport, credential or pairing), report per host: host identity, OS and architecture, and measured_at (UTC, the host's own clock) together with Central's received_at.

CPU is reported as logical CPU count and whole-host busy percent over a stated sampling window; on Unix the 1/5/15-minute load averages are also reported; on Windows load average is reported as unsupported rather than invented.

Memory is reported in bytes as total, in use excluding reclaimable cache, reclaimable cache (standby/file-backed/buff-cache), free, and available; on Windows also commit used and commit limit; values that a platform cannot measure are marked unsupported, never estimated.
Disk is reported in bytes, total and free, for each configured volume (at minimum the TermAl data volume and each runner checkout volume), with the mount or drive identity.

Network is reported per active interface as cumulative received and sent bytes with their counter timestamp, plus derived rates in bytes per second over a stated window when two samples exist; otherwise the rate is marked unavailable.

Each metric carries a state of available, stale (older than a documented threshold), unavailable (with a bounded reason, such as peer disconnected or probe error) or unsupported; a disconnected or unreachable peer appears as unavailable with its last-known snapshot labelled stale, never as zero or absent.

Collection is bounded and cheap: no shell-outs on the request path, no StateInner lock held while sampling, and a documented maximum response time; sampling never starts, stops or alters a test run or any other process.

The UI or a documented API shows the aggregate, and a feature brief in docs/features documents the metrics, units, freshness rules and platform differences, cross-linked with central-control-plane.md and native-mailbox-relay.md.
Tests cover snapshot shape and units, the stale and unavailable states for a disconnected peer, the unsupported markers per platform, and that the endpoint is read-only.
